A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SRA-CL research. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison across all pages, including v2's Appendices A–D and checklist. v1 has no separate appendix.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original recommendation experiments, including baseline comparisons, ablations, hyperparameter studies and sparsity analyses.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original recommendation experiments, while Appendix C adds item-synthesis and alternative-LLM results.

M1.justification: The retrieval framework, learnable user-sample synthesizer and backbone-only inference remain. However, v2 Equation (11) omits the reverse-direction term in v1 Equation (14), changing the specified intra-user loss. The displayed LLM prompts also change. These are reported specification changes; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use Yelp and Amazon Sports, Beauty and Office, with identical dataset statistics. The same Beauty/Office sequence-length groups support sparsity evaluation; no new dataset, domain or task scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: RLMRec is added to the overall comparison in v2 Tables 1 and 6. All twelve original baselines remain, so comparator coverage expands by one method.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation configurations using Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, retrieval without semantic information, bypassed LLM processing and learnable item synthesis. The existing data filtering, leave-one-out splits, full-catalog ranking, metric cutoffs and core training settings remain.

E4.justification: v2 Table 2 adds controls isolating semantic retrieval and LLM processing. Appendix C adds learnable versus non-learnable item synthesis and robustness across two LLMs, substantially expanding diagnostic coverage of central design choices. Conversely, the sparse-group NDCG panels from v1 Figure 7 are removed; v2 Figure 5 retains only HR.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run averages and paired t-tests at significance level 0.01. v2's checklist repeats this practice without adding seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: New result series cover RLMRec, semantic/LLM ablations, item-synthesis alternatives and Qwen, including small differences between LLMs and no consistent advantage from learnable item synthesis. Retained main SRA-CL scores are identical. Corrections include CoSeRec's Sports HR@20 from 0.0636 to 0.0638, DuoRec's Beauty NDCG@10 from 0.0444 to 0.0443, and the Sports unlearnable ablation from 0.792 to 0.0792. Sparse-group NDCG results are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of the intra-user loss changes from two directed logarithmic terms in v1 Equation (14) to one in v2 Equation (11). Other core definitions are equivalent or renumbered; neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The effectiveness, model-agnostic design and four-dataset claims remain. v2 adds a central criticism that fixed pairing rules prevent learning optimal positives, including the claim that identical-next-item pairing supplies no information beyond the recommendation objective. This refines the contribution's rationale without replacing the framework.

C2.justification: The synthesizer's rationale shifts from explicit semantic/ID-space misalignment toward user heterogeneity and fixed-rule limitations. v2 adds a possible model-size explanation for LLM differences and acknowledges that only two LLMs were tested. It also softens the assertion that item substitution preserves preferences to reducing semantic uncertainty.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and specifies 32 GB GPU memory. Its revised prompts include item descriptions in user inputs and 200/100-word summary limits; most training details and algorithms are retained or relocated. The added checklist's denial of an important LLM role conflicts with the method description.

R1.justification: v2 adds the RLMRec reference, removes the broad sequential-recommendation overview and associated citations, and drops v1 Section 2.3's claim to be the first work using LLMs to improve contrastive sequential recommendation. The main contrastive-learning and LLM research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method exposition are extensively rewritten, including cross-/intra-sequence terminology becoming inter-/intra-user. Backbone material moves into preliminaries, related work follows experiments, and technical material is reorganized into appendices. v2 also introduces an out-of-place reviewer-style paragraph under the conclusion.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column ACM layout to a single-column NeurIPS layout. Figures 1–2 are redrawn, the main comparison table is transposed and split, ablation columns and supplementary tables are added, and hyperparameter panels are regrouped by metric. Prompts move to the appendix, while sparse-group NDCG panels disappear.

improvement.justification: The new semantic/LLM controls in Table 2 and design checks in Appendix C strengthen evidence for previously insufficiently isolated components; the code link improves reproducibility information. These gains are tempered by the unexplained loss-formula change, removed sparse-group NDCG evidence, and new editorial inconsistencies, including the reviewer-style paragraph and contradictory LLM-use declaration.
